resources.title: Indiana Driver's Manual — Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals (PDF)
Indiana Driver's Manual — Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation (PDF)

intro: Indiana's knowledge exam has two parts — traffic maneuvers and traffic signs — and you need at least 80% on each. Our Indiana bank comes from the official Indiana Driver's Manual.

testTypes.name: Learner's permit / operator license
testTypes.description: The written knowledge exam with a traffic-signs section and a traffic-maneuvers section.

notes: The exam has multiple-choice questions in two sections: traffic maneuvers and traffic signs.
You need 80% or higher correct on each component. The BMV page we verified does not state the total number of questions, so our mock is scored at 80% overall.

mockPresets.label: Indiana practice exam
mockPresets.description: 40 mixed questions from signs and traffic maneuvers, scored at Indiana's official 80% passing rate.

commonMistakes.text: Hitting the brakes after a blowout. Indiana's manual says to ease off the gas and let the car slow down.
commonMistakes.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Tire Blowout

commonMistakes.text: Mixing up yield rules at all-way stops. When two vehicles arrive together, the vehicle on the left yields.
commonMistakes.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — All-Way Stops

commonMistakes.text: Studying only the rules. You also need 80% on the separate traffic signs section.

faq.q: What score do I need on the Indiana knowledge exam?
faq.a: 80% or higher on each of the two components — traffic maneuvers and traffic signs.

faq.q: How old must I be for an Indiana learner's permit?
faq.a: 15 if you are enrolled in driver education; 16 or older if you are not.

faq.q: How long is an Indiana learner's permit valid?
faq.a: Two years from the date of issuance. You must hold it for at least 180 days before applying for a license.

questions.question: How is Indiana's knowledge exam scored?
options: Two sections — traffic maneuvers and traffic signs — and you need 80% or higher on each
questions.correctAnswer: Two sections — traffic maneuvers and traffic signs — and you need 80% or higher on each
questions.explanation: The exam has multiple-choice questions in two sections (traffic maneuvers and traffic signs); you need 80% or higher correct on each component.
questions.sourceSection: Knowledge Exam

questions.question: If you are enrolled in an approved driver education program, how old must you be for an Indiana learner's permit?
questions.explanation: Applicants enrolled in driver education must be at least 15 years of age.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Obtaining a New Credential

questions.question: If you are not enrolled in driver education, how old must you be for an Indiana learner's permit?
questions.explanation: Applicants not enrolled in driver education must be 16 years of age or older.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Obtaining a New Credential

questions.question: How long is an Indiana learner's permit valid?
questions.correctAnswer: Two years
questions.explanation: Learner's permits are valid for two years from the date of issuance.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Obtaining a New Credential

questions.question: How long must you hold an Indiana learner's permit before applying for a license?
questions.correctAnswer: At least 180 days
questions.explanation: You must hold a learner's permit for at least 180 days before applying for a license.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Obtaining a New Credential

questions.question: How many hours of supervised driving practice does Indiana require before a probationary license?
options: At least 50 hours, including 10 at night
questions.correctAnswer: At least 50 hours, including 10 at night
questions.explanation: Applicants must complete at least 50 hours of supervised driving practice, including at least 10 hours at night.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Obtaining a New Credential

questions.question: An Indiana permit holder under 18 who is not in driver education may drive with which supervisor?
options: A licensed driver 25 or older, or a licensed spouse 21 or older
questions.correctAnswer: A licensed driver 25 or older, or a licensed spouse 21 or older
questions.explanation: The supervising driver must be a licensed driver at least 25 years old, or a spouse at least 21.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Obtaining a New Credential

questions.question: During the first 180 days of an Indiana probationary license, when may you NOT drive?
questions.correctAnswer: Between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.
questions.explanation: For the first 180 days, probationary drivers may not drive between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Obtaining a New Credential

questions.question: During the first 180 days of an Indiana probationary license, who may ride as a passenger?
options: Only a licensed person 25 or older, a spouse 21 or older, or immediate family
questions.correctAnswer: Only a licensed person 25 or older, a spouse 21 or older, or immediate family
questions.explanation: No passengers for the first 180 days except a licensed person 25 or older, a spouse 21 or older, and immediate family members.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Obtaining a New Credential

questions.question: In Indiana, brown traffic signs indicate:
questions.correctAnswer: Recreational and cultural interest sites
questions.explanation: Brown traffic signs indicate nearby recreational and cultural interest sites.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Colors

questions.question: In Indiana, blue traffic signs display:
questions.correctAnswer: Road services and information
questions.explanation: Blue traffic signs display road services and information.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Colors

questions.question: In Indiana, green traffic signs indicate:
questions.correctAnswer: Permitted movements, directions or guidance
questions.explanation: Green traffic signs indicate permitted movements and directions or guidance.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Colors

questions.question: In Indiana, orange traffic signs warn drivers about:
questions.correctAnswer: Temporary traffic conditions
questions.explanation: Orange traffic signs warn drivers of temporary traffic conditions.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Colors

questions.question: In Indiana, white traffic signs display:
options: Traffic regulations such as speed limits
questions.correctAnswer: Traffic regulations such as speed limits
questions.explanation: White traffic signs display traffic regulations, such as speed limits.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Colors

questions.question: In Indiana, red traffic signs convey regulations that require drivers to:
questions.correctAnswer: Take immediate action
questions.explanation: Red traffic signs convey traffic regulations that require drivers to take immediate action.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Colors

questions.question: In Indiana, circular traffic signs alert drivers to:
questions.correctAnswer: Upcoming railroad crossings
questions.explanation: Circular traffic signs alert drivers to upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Shapes

questions.question: Where are pennant-shaped signs posted in Indiana?
options: On the right side of one-way roads
On the left-hand side of two-way roads
questions.correctAnswer: On the left-hand side of two-way roads
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped traffic signs are posted on the left-hand side of two-way roads.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Shapes

questions.question: In Indiana, diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of:
questions.correctAnswer: Upcoming road conditions and hazards
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped traffic signs warn drivers of upcoming road conditions and hazards.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Shapes

questions.question: In Indiana, a five-sided traffic sign warns that you are:
options: Entering an area near a school
questions.correctAnswer: Entering an area near a school
questions.explanation: Five-sided traffic signs warn drivers that they are entering an area near a school.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Sign Shapes

questions.question: In Indiana, if you are facing a green light:
options: You have the right of way
You must yield to cross traffic
questions.correctAnswer: You have the right of way
questions.explanation: A green light means go; if you are facing a green light, you have the right of way.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Signals

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean in Indiana?
options: The green light has ended and the signal is about to turn red
questions.correctAnswer: The green light has ended and the signal is about to turn red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means the green light has ended and the signal is about to turn red.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Signals

questions.question: In Indiana, a yellow flashing arrow for a turn means:
options: You have the right of way
You may turn only after yielding
questions.correctAnswer: You may turn only after yielding
questions.explanation: A yellow flashing arrow means you may proceed with the turn only after you have yielded.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 6: Traffic Signs and Signals — Traffic Signals

questions.question: In Indiana, when may you cross a solid yellow line?
questions.correctAnswer: Only to turn
questions.explanation: You may cross a broken yellow line to pass when safe, but you should not cross a solid yellow line except to turn.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Lane Markings

questions.question: After passing in Indiana, you must return to the right side of the road no less than how far before any oncoming vehicle?
questions.correctAnswer: 100 feet
questions.explanation: You must return to the right side of the road no less than 100 feet before any oncoming vehicle.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Passing Other Vehicles

questions.question: In Indiana, you may not pass within 100 feet of:
options: An intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct or tunnel
questions.correctAnswer: An intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct or tunnel
questions.explanation: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct or tunnel.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Prohibited Passing

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an Indiana interstate, what should you do?
options: Make a U-turn through the median
Proceed to the next exit and re-enter
questions.correctAnswer: Proceed to the next exit and re-enter
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on an interstate highway; proceed to the next exit and re-enter.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — U-Turns

questions.question: At an Indiana all-way stop, who proceeds first?
options: The first vehicle to stop at the intersection
questions.correctAnswer: The first vehicle to stop at the intersection
questions.explanation: The first vehicle to stop at the intersection is the first to proceed.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — All-Way Stops

questions.question: At an Indiana all-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time:
options: The vehicle on the right yields
The vehicle on the left yields
questions.correctAnswer: The vehicle on the left yields
questions.explanation: When vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left yields the right-of-way.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — All-Way Stops

questions.question: In an Indiana roundabout, traffic moves:
options: Counterclockwise, entering and exiting only with right turns
questions.correctAnswer: Counterclockwise, entering and exiting only with right turns
questions.explanation: In a roundabout, traffic enters or exits only through right turns and proceeds counterclockwise.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Roundabouts

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for passenger vehicles on Indiana rural interstates (unless posted lower)?
questions.correctAnswer: 70 mph
questions.explanation: Passenger vehicles may not exceed 70 mph or the posted limit on rural interstates.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Speed Limits

questions.question: What is the speed limit on an Indiana urban interstate (unless posted otherwise)?
questions.correctAnswer: 55 mph
questions.explanation: On an urban interstate highway, vehicles may not exceed 55 mph or the posted speed.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Speed Limits

questions.question: In most Indiana urban residential areas, the speed limit is:
questions.correctAnswer: 30 mph
questions.explanation: In most urban residential areas, vehicles may not exceed 30 mph or the posted speed.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Speed Limits

questions.question: What is the speed limit in Indiana alleys (unless posted otherwise)?
questions.correctAnswer: 15 mph
questions.explanation: In alleys, vehicles may not exceed 15 mph or the posted speed limit.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Speed Limits

questions.question: Indiana's manual recommends staying at least how far behind the vehicle ahead?
questions.correctAnswer: Two to three seconds
questions.explanation: Stay at least two to three seconds behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Following Distance

questions.question: In Indiana, what must you do when you approach a school bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm extended?
questions.correctAnswer: Stop
questions.explanation: You must stop when you approach a school bus with flashing red lights activated and stop arm extended.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — School Buses

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches in Indiana, you must:
options: Yield, move to the right and come to a complete stop
questions.correctAnswer: Yield, move to the right and come to a complete stop
questions.explanation: Motorists must yield the right of way, move over to the right and come to a complete stop.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: Which vehicles must always stop at railroad crossings in Indiana?
options: School buses and vehicles carrying passengers for hire
questions.correctAnswer: School buses and vehicles carrying passengers for hire
questions.explanation: All school buses and all vehicles carrying passengers for hire must stop at railroad crossings.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 7: Safe Vehicle Operation — Railroad Crossings

questions.question: If you are involved in a crash in Indiana, you must:
options: Leave if no one is hurt
Stop immediately at or as close as possible to the scene
Drive to the nearest police station first
questions.correctAnswer: Stop immediately at or as close as possible to the scene
questions.explanation: The driver of a vehicle involved in an accident must stop immediately or as close as possible to the scene.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — What To Do After an Accident

questions.question: In Indiana, when should you NOT move your vehicle after a crash?
options: When the crash involves injury, death or entrapment
When it is on the shoulder
questions.correctAnswer: When the crash involves injury, death or entrapment
questions.explanation: Do not move the vehicle if the accident results in injury, death or entrapment.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Should You Move Your Vehicle?

questions.question: If a crash in Indiana injures another person, the driver is required to:
questions.correctAnswer: Provide reasonable assistance
questions.explanation: If the accident results in injury or death, the driver must provide reasonable assistance.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Provide Reasonable Assistance

questions.question: According to Indiana's manual, what three things can you do to avoid a collision?
options: Stop quickly, turn quickly, speed up
questions.correctAnswer: Stop quickly, turn quickly, speed up
questions.explanation: Depending on the situation, you can stop quickly, turn quickly or speed up.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Avoiding Collisions

questions.question: If your wheels drift onto the shoulder in Indiana, you should:
options: Not turn back onto the pavement right away
questions.correctAnswer: Not turn back onto the pavement right away
questions.explanation: If your wheels drift onto the shoulder, do not try to turn back onto the pavement right away.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Driving off the Pavement

questions.question: If your vehicle plunges into water, Indiana's manual says to:
options: Remove your seat belt and open a window instead of trying to open a door
questions.correctAnswer: Remove your seat belt and open a window instead of trying to open a door
questions.explanation: Do not attempt to open a door. Remove your seat belt and open a window.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Plunging into Water

questions.question: In Indiana, how far behind your disabled vehicle should a red reflective triangle be placed on level road?
questions.correctAnswer: 200 feet
questions.explanation: Place your red reflective triangle 200 feet behind your vehicle (500 feet if you are on a hill).
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations

questions.question: If you must exit your vehicle on a roadside shoulder in Indiana, exit:
questions.correctAnswer: On the passenger side
questions.explanation: If you must exit while on a roadside shoulder, exit on the passenger side.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Roadside Emergency Situations

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout in Indiana, you should:
options: Take your foot off the gas and let the car slow down without braking
questions.correctAnswer: Take your foot off the gas and let the car slow down without braking
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the gas pedal, do not apply the brakes, and let the car slow down.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Tire Blowout

questions.question: If your brakes fail, Indiana's manual says to:
options: Shift to a lower gear if possible and pump the brake pedal fast and hard
questions.correctAnswer: Shift to a lower gear if possible and pump the brake pedal fast and hard
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear if possible and pump the brake pedal fast and hard several times.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Brake Failure

questions.question: When a police officer signals you to stop in Indiana, how can you acknowledge the officer?
options: Turn on your right turn signal
questions.correctAnswer: Turn on your right turn signal
questions.explanation: Acknowledge the officer's presence by turning on your right turn signal.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Traffic Stops by Law Enforcement

questions.question: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, Indiana's manual says to never:
options: Let your engine run in a closed garage
questions.correctAnswer: Let your engine run in a closed garage
questions.explanation: Never let your vehicle's engine run in a closed garage.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Accidents and Emergency Situations — Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
